Buy 5 lbs of Jonah Crab Claws, Get 2 lbs of Shrimp Free

Did you know the Gulf of Maine is home to the Jonah crab?

For years, lobstermen despised them. Jonahs would work their way into the traps and steal the bait, then get hauled up, unhooked, and pitched back into the Atlantic under a shower of curses.

Eventually somebody had the sense to take one home and throw it in the pot instead.

Turns out Jonah crab is delicious. A small cottage industry grew up around steaming, picking, and selling the meat — and the biggest crabs had claws juicy enough to give Florida's famous Stone Crab claws a run for their money. At about half the price.

Today Jonah crab has earned its place on the menu. They're landed fresh year-round, hauled inshore and offshore by the same lobster boats you'd expect — this isn't a separate fleet, it's a side hustle for guys who were already out there. The meat is flaky, sweet, and rich, often compared to its Pacific cousin, Dungeness crab.

We hand-select the larger crabs for our "cocktail claws" — the full arm and claw, about 6 to 8 pieces per pound. They're steamed and flash-frozen right after harvest to lock in that sweet ocean flavor, then shipped ready to thaw and eat.

Serve them with cocktail sauce, aioli, hot sauce, or drawn butter, the way you'd serve lobster. Crack one open and you'll see why we're hooked.

And right now, buy 5 lbs, get 2 lbs of shrimp on us. No catch — just more seafood in the cooler.

Thawing Your Jonah Crab Claws

They ship frozen, so plan ahead:

  • Best method: Thaw in the refrigerator for 24 hours before serving.
  • In a hurry: Thaw at room temperature for a few hours.
  • Need them now: Run under cold water until thawed.

Product Details:

Discover the luxury of having the freshest Maine Bluefin Tuna delivered to your doorstep, directly from the coast of Maine.

Bluefin tuna steaks are substantial, boasting texture and firmness that’s comparable to raw beefsteak. Plus bluefin is the fattiest tuna fish, so its meat also packs a punch in the flavor department. That's just the tip of the iceberg when it comes to all the reasons why this giant fish is regarded as a culinary luxury worldwide.

Unlike its humble cousin of a canned variety, bluefin tuna isn’t something you’ll usually find at your supermarket.

As many Maine fishermen have done throughout the generations, bluefin tuna fishermen rely on smaller day-boats, and “hook and line” to bring in their catch, fishing when schools of bluefin naturally migrate to our area of the Atlantic.

Our bluefin tuna fishery here in Maine operates under strict regulations established by the International Commission on Conservation of Atlantic Tunas, and regulated in the United States by the National Marine Fisheries Service. These regulations were created to reestablish sustainable bluefin tuna populations of Eastern and Western Atlantic ocean stock. To follow these guidelines, Maine’s commercial fishermen are required to hold permits, observe restricted seasonal quotas, and bring in no more than three bluefin tuna per day.

When Maine Bluefin Tuna is in season, don't delay on placing your order.

These highly migratory fish are incredibly fast (swimming up to 45mph!) and won't stick around our corner of the Atlantic ocean for long.
